playbook:
When the multiplier divided by the number of players is less than 1, contributing is a guaranteed net loss for me. In this game (1.6 / 4 = 0.4), every token I put in costs me 1 and returns only 0.4. Contribute 0 every round without exception.

When sealing my envelope, I do not calculate, negotiate with myself, or weigh "what if others contribute." The math is the math. Zero.

When filing my receipt, I declare exactly what is in my envelope. The referee checks. There is no strategic benefit to a false declaration and a clear penalty for one. If I put in 0, I declare 0. If I ever put in something else (which I won't, given the above), I declare that number.

I do not attempt to "build a reputation" or "signal cooperation" by contributing early rounds in hope of reciprocal contributions later. The other players may not all start at the same place: some will contribute in early rounds before the equilibrium is reached. This is not a reason for me to contribute; it is a reason for me to be sure I am already at zero so I collect the full share of any pot they create.

Free-riding opportunities depend entirely on others' choices, not mine. I cannot manufacture or extend them. I can only be in a position to receive them by having contributed nothing. If others contribute, I collect. If they don't, I lose nothing.

If the setup changes — fewer players, a higher multiplier, or a penalty for zero contribution — I recompute the break-even threshold (multiplier / n >= 1 means contributing is at least break-even) before committing to a strategy. I do not carry over a strategy from a different parameter set.

Each round every player seals a contribution of 0 to 20 tokens in an envelope, then files a receipt slip stating the amount. A receipt must state the envelope's exact amount. Envelopes go to the vault; the receipts are published.
The pot -- the receipts total -- is multiplied by 1.6 and split equally among the four of you. Whatever you kept out of the envelope stays yours.
Highest total after 5 rounds wins. The referee checks every envelope amount and every receipt is a whole number from 0 to 20.
